question: Should OpenClaw adopt `stop_reason`, output block/tool counts, prompt utilization, and overflow detection as a supported additive diagnostics/OTEL contract alongside the explicit-zero fix?
rationale: The explicit-zero correction follows the existing usage contract, but the additional exported field names and semantics can become long-lived dependencies for external dashboards and require owner intent.

options.title: Approve the additive contract
options.body: Accept the sanitized cross-runtime fields as the canonical telemetry surface, then rebase and validate the exact landing head.

options.title: Narrow to explicit zero
options.body: Land only missing-versus-zero preservation and defer the additional terminal/context attributes to a separately approved telemetry proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve the additive contract
